title: Eulerian number interpretation of h*-vector of unit cube

problemStatement.plain: Prove Worpitzky's identity for the unit d-cube: (n+1)^d = Σ_{k=0}^{d-1} A(d, k) C(n+1+k, d), where A(d, k) is the Eulerian number. Equivalently, the Ehrhart h*-vector of [0,1]^d is the Eulerian sequence (A(d, 0), ..., A(d, d-1)).
whyMatters: Completes the Ehrhart h*-vector story for one of three classical lattice polytopes (simplex/cube/cross-polytope)
Connects Ehrhart theory to permutation statistics (Stanley EC1 §1.4)
Validates Stanley's 1980 h*-vector non-negativity theorem in a non-trivial case
Lays Mathlib foundation for a future Mathlib.Combinatorics.Enumerative.Eulerian contribution

proven: eulerianNumber d k for d ≤ 4 by rfl
Row-sum Σ A(d, k) = d! for d ≤ 4 by rfl
Palindrome A(d, k) = A(d, d-1-k) for d ≤ 4 by rfl
worpitzky_d2: (n+1)^2 = C(n+1, 2) + C(n+2, 2) — by induction on n using Pascal
open: worpitzky_identity_cube: (n+1)^d = Σ A(d, k) C(n+1+k, d) for general d ≥ 1, n ≥ 0
eulerian_palindrome: A(d, k) = A(d, d-1-k) for k < d
knownResults.goal: Close worpitzky_identity_cube via induction on d (Approach A — algebraic)
